description: lib.rs:193 and lib.rs:211 place #[must_use] on trait method declarations. In Rust, #[must_use] on a trait method does NOT automatically propagate to concrete implementations — the attribute is only enforced when the method is called through the trait (dyn RevocationChecker or generic T: RevocationChecker). Callers using a concrete CrlChecker or OcspChecker directly (without indirection through the trait) will NOT get the must_use lint. This creates a false sense of safety: the annotation suggests the result is always checked, but it may be silently dropped in non-generic contexts. Fix: document this limitation in the trait doc comment, OR (preferred) rely on the caller using must_use at the call site (e.g. verify_chain). The annotation is not wrong, but its limited scope should be noted.
notes: False positive: Rust #[must_use] on trait method DOES propagate to call sites through concrete impls. No action needed.
title: #[must_use] on RevocationChecker trait methods is not inherited by overrides — misleading placement
